record.question: How should Blaster improve verification without weakening the existing evidence boundary?

options.strongest_objection: Requires a versioned backend bridge, exact dependency pins and explicit supported replay types
Blaster unknown can be a warning and successful tactics use a trusted axiom
A major prover project would delay useful counterexample discovery

requirements.statement: Only nonempty, unique, complete expected results with a valid domain witness pass; solver trust cannot satisfy a kernel policy
requirements.counterexample: An unknown command exits zero, a warning is suppressed, a witness fails or a duplicate/missing result is accepted

requirements.statement: Receipts bind the complete tracked project input set, manifest, exact tool and dependency revisions and retained logs; drift refuses
requirements.counterexample: Editing a referenced definition, changing polarity or modifying the installed backend preserves a passing receipt

requirements.statement: Unexpected falsifications enter the existing cex ledger; pins require a tracked concrete regression, exact scalar bindings and a fresh successful specialization of the original property
requirements.counterexample: A printed model, altered input, stale receipt or unsupported model closes a counterexample without replay

requirements.statement: Imported Blaster tactic trust is visible to the hatch scan and standalone #blaster/#bmc/#kind obligations have statement identities
requirements.counterexample: The original imported tactic and command-only scanner probes still produce zero coverage

checks.scope: Execute the adapter CLI against a controlled backend boundary, source scanners, dependency/input freshness and concrete counterexample replay/pinning. Separate actual Lean/Z3 validation is recorded in the change evidence.
assumptions: Fixture results establish adapter enforcement, not correctness of Blaster normalization or SMT translation
The host process runner and reviewed gate code are trusted; optional backend results retain solver trust

challenges.claim: Does a successful Lean build establish a kernel-checked Blaster theorem?
challenges.resolution: No. The adapter only accepts explicit solver trust; kernel policy refuses. Existing headline assumption audit remains available and imported tactic use gets a source category.

challenges.claim: Can arbitrary solver terms be pasted into a regression and trusted as replay?
challenges.resolution: No. Reification is restricted to explicitly typed Nat, Int, Bool and String bindings. Opaque models stay open; supported bindings specialize the original registered property and are rechecked before a pin is accepted.

challenges.claim: Does this implement all compiled Cardano ledger and protocol models?
challenges.resolution: This slice supplies the shared trustworthy backend and replay plumbing. Compiled UPLC and ledger models remain a separately scoped later integration, with fuel/conformance requirements from the assessment.
